title: NAMESAKES: Probing Identity Memorization in Text-to-Image Models
abstract: arXiv:2606.20155v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Text-to-image (T2I) models generate realistic likenesses of some individuals when prompted with their names, raising privacy concerns. However, distinguishing whether a generated face is memorized or fabricated currently requires ground-truth photos, access to training data, or white-box access to model internals, limiting applicability. We introduce a fully black-box behavioral probe that distinguishes between memorized and unrecognized names, while requiring no reference photos or prior knowledge of training data. To benchmark this task, we present the NAMESAKES dataset of over one thousand names and faces of public figures spanning a wide range of fame levels, along with perturbed, less famous names. Experiments on state-of-the-art T2I models show that our probe substantially predicts identity memorization and separates memorized from unrecognized names, with further insights into differences across model families.

translated_title: 同名者（NAMESAKES）：探测文生图模型中的身份记忆
translated_abstract: 文生图（T2I）模型在输入某些人的名字时能够生成他们的逼真肖像，这引发了隐私方面的担忧。然而，目前要区分生成的人脸是模型记忆的还是凭空捏造的，需要真实照片、训练数据的访问权限，或对模型内部的白盒访问，这限制了其适用性。我们提出了一种完全黑盒的行为探测方法，能够区分被记忆的名字和未被识别的名字，且无需参考照片或对训练数据的先验知识。为对该任务进行基准测试，我们构建了NAMESAKES数据集，其中包含一千多个公众人物的名字和面孔，涵盖广泛的知名度范围，还包括经过扰动的、知名度较低的名字。在最先进的文生图模型上的实验表明，我们的探测方法能有效预测身份记忆，并将被记忆的名字与未被识别的名字区分开来，同时还深入揭示了不同模型家族之间的差异。
tldr: 该论文提出了一种无需参考照片或训练数据知识的完全黑盒行为探测方法及涵盖一千多名公众人物的NAMESAKES数据集，用于区分文生图模型生成的人脸是记忆的真实身份还是凭空捏造，以应对隐私风险。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces a fully black-box behavioral probe and the NAMESAKES dataset of over one thousand public figures to distinguish whether faces generated by text-to-image models are memorized identities or fabrications, without requiring reference photos or training-data knowledge.
